info.bio:
Hay dos bandas con éste nombre:

1.) Banda Speed Metal de Düsseldorf, Alemania, formada en 1983.

2.) Warrant es una banda de glam metal de Los Ángeles, California, formada en 1984, que obtuvo su mayor éxito durante los noventa con su single y álbum "Cherry Pie".

Es el estilo creado durante finales de los 80s y comienzos de los 90s el que realmente representa el sello de esta banda. El estigma de la banda era un heavy metal duro, "cheesy", obsesionado con el sexo y normalmente relacionado con un perverso sentido del humor.

scenes.name: Metal de los noventa: progresivo, death y black metal
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Si los ochenta fueron la edad de oro del heavy metal, los noventa lo fragmentan en estilos que amplían ideas anteriores. El pop-metal (Warrant, Extreme, Live) es lo menos significativo; Marilyn Manson casa el scum-rock de Alice Cooper con el industrial de Nine Inch Nails. El metal progresivo (Warrior Soul, Dream Theater, Royal Hunt, Opeth, los suizos Alboth!). El death metal muta en algo más terrible y más musical gracias a Brutal Truth, Cannibal Corpse y, sobre todo, la tríada de Type O Negative (Slow Deep And Hard, misas negras wagnerianas), Today Is The Day y Fear Factory; Biohazard, Coalesce, Dillinger Escape Plan. El nuevo black metal escandinavo: Entombed, Darkthrone, Immortal, Mayhem, Enslaved, Emperor, Satyricon, Cradle Of Filth.

podcast.title: Decline of "Cheesy Pop Metal" (1991)
podcast.body: Anthony Kiedis, in his autobiography "Scar Tissue," identified Warrant as one of the "cheesy pop metal bands" that were "finished" by 1991, signaling a changing of the musical guard. "Cheesy pop metal bands like Warren's and Poison and Skid Row were finished."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Escape from Rehab (June 26, 1996)
xref.body: After being transferred to Impact House, a residential drug treatment facility, for what was supposed to be a six-month stay, Scott Wyland disappeared on June 26, 1996. An arrest warrant was issued for him. "But then on June 26th, Wyland disappeared."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Return to Court (1996)
xref.body: Before he could be located by the warrant, Scott Wyland reappeared "safe and sober" at the Pasadena Municipal Court, explaining his disappearance as a need to speak with his wife about a personal problem. "Wyland turned up safe and sober at the Pasadena Municipal Court."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Disappearance from Courthouse (July 9, 1998)
xref.body: On the morning of Thursday, July 9, 1998, Scott Wyland was last seen smoking cigarettes and answering questions on the steps of the Los Angeles County Courthouse. Upon hearing about the $250,000 arrest warrant, he vanished, knowing he would be arrested if he entered the building. "He knew that he'd be arrested the second he put inside, so he vanished."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: LA Drug Purchase Arrest (July 22, 1998)
xref.body: At 6:30 PM on Tuesday, July 22, 1998, Scott Wyland was arrested at 6th and Burlington Street near downtown Los Angeles for simply buying drugs, rather than on the outstanding arrest warrant. Drugs were found on his person. "The police weren't looking for him because of that arrest warrant. They picked him up because he was simply buying drugs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Missed LA Court Dates (June/July 1998)
xref.body: Judge Larry Fiddler in Los Angeles, assigned to Wyland's case, required him to appear at court hearings to monitor his sobriety. Wyland missed a June 11 hearing (excused as he was in rehab) and a subsequent early June appearance, prompting Judge Fiddler to issue a $250,000 arrest warrant. "Wylandt missed the first hearing on June 11th, but he had an excuse. He was in a drug rehab facility."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Influence of Jane's Addiction
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins cited Jane's Addiction as a major influence that changed his musical direction in high school. Prior to hearing them, he listened to older classic rock and new wave, but Jane's Addiction's raw, "disgusting," and "awesome" style resonated with him, inspiring him to be like them. "And then when I heard Jane's addiction, because I was really... It was all warrant and all that kind of crap, you know."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Jane's Addiction as Personal "Punk Rock"
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins was disillusioned with the "blah music" of hair metal (like Warrant) during his high school years. Hearing Jane's Addiction was a transformative experience, as he found them "disgusting," "awesome," and "scary," providing a raw energy that resonated with him much like punk rock did for others. "And then I heard Jane's addiction and it was like, dude, I could play like the dudes in the poster. But they were a mess and they were disgusting and they were awesome and they were scary."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
